options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: An audiometer is a medical instrument mainly used to test a person’s hearing ability (auditory capacity). Through head-phones, it produces sound signals at different frequencies and checks the minimum level at which the patient can hear. The level is indicated on the decibel scale, but it is calibrated relative to the average human hearing threshold, not as a direct measurement of an external sound source. Therefore, an audiometer is used to assess hearing sensitivity, not to measure the physical intensity of an outside sound source directly.

stem: Which of the following energy changes involves frictional force?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Frictional force acts both in stationary and in moving conditions. The coefficients related to friction are called the coefficient of static friction and the coefficient of kinetic friction. In a stationary condition, there is no displacement; hence no work is done and no energy conversion takes place. But in a moving condition, motion occurs against friction, due to which energy is lost in the form of heat. In other words, kinetic energy is converted into heat energy.

stem: For a body moving with constant speed in a horizontal circle, which of the following remains constant?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: When a body is moving with uniform speed in a horizontal circle, its kinetic energy K= mv2 remains constant. When a body moves in a horizontal circle, only the direction of velocity, acceleration, and force keeps changing continuously at every instant, but there is no change in their magnitudes. The capacity of an object to do work due to its motion is called its kinetic energy.

stem: A pair of Oxen exerts a force of 140 Newtons while ploughing the field. The field ploughed is 15 metres long. The work done in ploughing the length of the field is:
expl: In physics, the work done (Work) by a constant force is given as follows when force and displacement are in the same direction: W = F × s Where: • F = applied force (in N) • s = displacement / distance (in m) • W = work done (in J) Given in the question: • F = 140 N • Length of the field (displacement) = 15 m • The oxen pull the plough along the length of the field. Therefore, force and displacement are in the same direction, so: W = 140 × 15 = 2100 J Hence, the work done in pulling the plough through a length of 15 m is 2100 J.
